description_en: The Prajāpati community of Kathmandu's Jyāthā reveres Lord Viśvakarmā at this temple in the form of Gaṇeśa, their lineage deity. The annual alms-giving ceremony,pañcadāna, takes place here on the 13th of the dark fortnight of Bhādra.Located in a courtyard west of the Jyāthā Gaṇeśa temple (KAT0240) in Jyāthā Ṭola, Kathmandu, the Viśvakarmā Temple faces south. It features a single-tiered brass roof topped with a brass finial from which a brass oblong banner (patāḥ) hangs. Metal flags stand on either side of the sanctum's entrance, but there is notoranaabove the door. Inside, the main deity is a stone statue of Gaṇeśa covered in brass, standing on a shrew with his left foot in thepratyalidhaposture (right leg bent). Despite being called the Viśvakarmā temple, the sanctum houses Gaṇeśa, not Viśvakarmā. A brasstoranadepicting a flying Garuḍa adorns the deity, and above it is another brasstoranafeaturing Gaṇeśa. To the east of the temple, a recently donated bell hangs on a stand.There is no historical evidence detailing the construction of this temple. The earliest inscription, dating back to 1798 CE (NS 918), mentions that individuals named Prajāpati Jeta, Amita, and Dhana, among others, collectively built aphalcarest house to the east of the temple for their lineage deity Viśvakarmā. Likewise, in 1814 CE (NS 934), the Aṣṭamī Sevā Guthi, a religious trust of 28 people from the Jyāthā Ṭola, constructed another rest house (sataḥ) in front of the temple. Later, in 1829 CE (NS 949), individuals including Beṣāsiṃha, Dhanaontasiṃha, and Dhanasiddhi built anotherphalcaand installed an inscription bearing their own figures.Again, in 1846 CE (NS 966), a donor built aphalcain memory of his deceased father, Mahaṃtasī, his mother, wife, and son. In 1853 CE (NS 973), Matyaṃsiṃ Prajāpati and his wife, Manamati, along with their sons and grandsons, replaced the old, worn-out statue of Viśvakarmā with a new one, wishing for the eternal peace of their deceased family members. They also established a religious trust with land and money for the statue’s anniversary rituals.In 1881 CE (NS 1001), the Digusivā Guthi, a religious trust responsible for serving the Prajāpati community's lineage deity, headed by Cidhisiṃha, renovated the dilapidated statue of Viśvakarmā and gilded it. In 2011 CE (VS 2068), the Pañcadāna Guthi of the Prajāpatis in Jyāthā, with financial assistance from the Kathmandu Metropolitan City, renovated the dilapidated temple.The Prajāpatis, the potter caste of the Newars, in Jyāthā believe themselves to be descendants of King Jayasthiti Malla. The king, it is said, married a commoner and granted their son 365ropanīs of land in various locations, allowing him to use oneropanīeach day (M. Prajāpati NS 1136, p. 59). This endowment is believed to be the foundation of the financial stability of the Viśvakarmā Guthi, the religious trust of the Jyāthā Prajāpatis.The cultural life of the Jyāthā Prajāpatis centers around the Viśvakarmā temple. They traditionally visit this temple to offer prayers during festivals and life-cycle rituals. They venerate the temple's Gaṇeśa statue as Viśvakarmā, the deity of skill and craftsmanship, whom they consider their lineage deity.*The most significant socio-religious event for the Jyāthā Prajāpatis of Kathmandu is the offering of alms, known aspañcadāna. This practice is managed by a dedicated religious trust. Preparations begin after Vajrācārya priests from Jhvāḥ Bāhāḥ (KAT0210) arrive to worship the Prajñāpāramitā manuscript on the 10th of the dark fortnight of Śrāvaṇa. Rice for the alms-giving ceremony is cooked on the 12th of the same fortnight, and the alms are offered to Śākyas and Vajrācāryas the following day. On the 14th, a feast calledmūbhvay(the main feast) was traditionally held for all trust members, but this has now been replaced with a meal ofsamaybaji, a traditional Newar food set. Thepañcadānatrust is believed to have been established in 1830 CE (NS 950).Each year, on the 2nd of the bright fortnight of Bhādra, the Jyāthā Prajāpatis perform esoteric worship of Viśvakarmā in the form of Gaṇeśa, which includes the sacrifice of two sheep and a subsequent feast. They also observe an annual worship of Nāsaḥdyaḥ, the deity of music and charm, though there is no fixed date for this ritual. The trust members choose a convenient Sunday or Thursday during the winter months to perform this worship.* Jyāthā, a locality inhabited by Prajāpati potters, exists in Kathmandu, Lalitpur, and Bhaktapur. The Prajāpatis in all three cities revere Gaṇeśa as Viśvakarmā (see Jeṭhā Gaṇeśa Mandira;BKT0510). An inscription referring to the Gaṇeśa of Patan’s Jyāthā Ṭola as Viśvakarmā can be found in D. Vajrācārya VS 2056, p. 93, inscr. no. 50.
description_ne: काठमाडौं, ज्याथाका प्रजापतिहरूले कुलदेवताको रूपमा पुज्ने गणेश रूपी विश्वकर्मा मन्दिर परिसरमा भाद्र कृष्ण १३ मा पञ्चदान प्रदान गरिन्छ ।काठमाडौंको ज्याथा टोलमा अवस्थित ज्याथा गणेश मन्दिर (KAT0240) को पश्चिमपट्टि रहेको चोकभित्र विश्वकर्मा मन्दिर निर्माण गरिएको छ । दक्षिणाभिमुख गरी निर्माण गरिएको यस मन्दिरमा एक तह पित्तलको छाना राखिएको छ । छानामाथि पित्तलको गजूर राखिएको छ । गजूरदेखि छानासम्म पुग्ने गरी पित्तलको पता: झुण्ड्याइएको छ । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकाको दायाँबायाँ धातुका झण्डा राखिएका छन्, तर ढोकामाथि तोरण राखिएको छैन । गर्भगृहभित्र बायाँ खुट्टाले छुचुन्द्रोमाथि टेकेर प्रत्यालिढ आसनमा उभिएको गणेशको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । यसलाई विश्वकर्मा मन्दिर भनिएपनि मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र विश्वकर्मा नभई गणेशको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । गणेशको मूर्ति ढुङ्गाले बनेको भएपनि बाहिर पित्तलको पाताले मोडिएको छ । गणेशलाई उडिरहेको गरूड अङ्कित पित्तलको तोरण चढाइएको छ । त्यसभन्दा माथि गणेश अङ्कित पित्तलको अर्को तोरण चढाइएको छ । मन्दिरको पूर्वमा हालसालै चढाइएको एउटा घण्टा रहेको छ ।यो मन्दिरको निर्माणबारे जानकारी दिने ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण उपलब्ध छैन । मन्दिर परिसरमा पाइएका अभिलेखमध्ये सबैभन्दा पुरानो नेसं ९१८ (सन् १७९८) को शिलापत्र हो जसमा प्रजापति जेत, अमित, धन लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर इष्टदेवता (विश्वकर्मा) को लागि मन्दिरको पूर्वमा फल्चा निर्माण गरेको कुरा लेखिएको छ । नेसं ९३४ (सन् १८१४) मा ज्याथा टोलका २८ जनाको अष्टमी सेवा गुठीले मन्दिर अगाडि सतः निर्माण गरेको थियो । नेसं ९४९ (सन् १८२९) मा बेषासिं, धनओन्तसिं, धनसिद्धि लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर फल्चा निर्माण गरी आफ्नो प्रतिमा अङ्कित शिलापत्र स्थापना गरेका थिए । त्यस्तै नेसं ९६६ (सन् १८४६) मा दिवंगत भएका बुबा महंतसी लगायत आमा, श्रीमती र छोराको मोक्षको कामना गरी एकजना दाताले फल्चा निर्माण गरिदिएका थिए । नेसं ९७३ (सन् १८५३) मा मत्यंसिं प्रजापति र उनकी श्रीमती मनमतिले छोरा, नातिहरूसँग मिलेर दिवंगत परिवारका सदस्यहरूको मोक्ष कामना गरी विश्वकर्माको पुरानो मूर्ति जीर्ण भएकोले त्यसको ठाउँमा नयाँ मूर्ति स्थापना गरिदिएका थिए । उनीहरूले मूर्तिको वर्षवर्द्धनपूजा गर्नको लागि खेत र केही रकमको कोष पनि स्थापना गरिदिएका थिए । नेसं १००१ (सन् १८८१) मा विश्वकर्माको मूर्ति जीर्ण भएकोले चिधिसिं प्रमुख रहेको दिगुसिवा गुठी (प्रजापतिहरूको कुलदेवता सेवा गर्ने गुठी) ले जीर्णोद्धार गरेको थियो । जीर्णोद्धार गरेपछि मूर्तिलाई सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको थियो । मन्दिर जीर्ण भएकोले विसं २०६८ (सन् २०११) मा ज्याथामा रहेका प्रजापतिहरूको पञ्चदान गुठीले जीर्णोद्धार गरेको थियो । जीर्णोद्धार गर्नको लागि काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाले पनि आर्थिक सहयोग गरेको थियो ।ज्याथाका प्रजापतिहरू आफूलाई जयस्थिति मल्लका सन्तान ठान्छन् । जयस्थिति मल्लले सर्वसाधारण प्रजासँग विवाह गरी उनीबाट जन्मेका छोरालाई प्रत्येक दिन एक रोपनीको दरले उपभोग गर्न पाउने गरी विभिन्न ठाउँमा ३६५ रोपनी जग्गाको व्यवस्था गरिदिएका थिए (M. Prjāpati NS 1136, p. 59) । त्यसैले ज्याथाका प्रजापतिहरूको विश्वकर्मा गुठी आर्थिक रूपले सम्पन्न मानिन्छ ।काठमाडौंका ज्याथा टोलमा बसोबास गर्ने प्रजापति (कुम्हाले)हरूको संस्कृतिको केन्द्रविन्दु यही विश्वकर्मा मन्दिर हो । उनीहरूको कुनै पनि चाडपर्व, भोजभतेर वा संस्कारजन्य कार्य गर्दा सबभन्दा पहिले यहीँ आएर पूजा गर्नुपर्ने परम्परा छ । उनीहरू गणेशलाई सीप सिकाउने देवता विश्वकर्माको रूपमा मान्छन् र आफ्नो कुलदेवता मानेर पूजा गर्छन् ।*ज्याथाका प्रजापतिहरूको सबैभन्दा मुख्य धार्मिक गतिविधि नै पञ्चदान प्रदान गर्नु हो । त्यसको लागि ज्याथ पञ्चदान गुठी गठन गरिएको छ । पञ्चदानको लागि श्रावण कृष्ण १० मा झ्वाः बाहाः (KAT0210) का वज्राचार्य आएर प्रज्ञापारमिता ग्रन्थ पूजा गरेपछि तयारी शुरु गरिन्छ । भाद्र कृष्ण १२ मा पञ्चदान दिनको लागि भुजा पकाइन्छ । भोलिपल्ट भाद्र कृष्ण १३ मा शाक्य-वज्राचार्यहरूलाई पञ्चदान दिइन्छ । पञ्चदानको भोलिपल्ट भाद्र कृष्ण १४ को दिनमामूभ्वय्भनी गुठीयाहरू सबैलाई भोज खुवाइन्थ्यो, अहिले समय्‌बजि मात्र खुवाइन्छ । यो गुठी नेसं ९५० (सन् १८३०) देखि शुरु भएको मानिन्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष भाद्र शुक्ल २ को दिनमा गणेश रूपी विश्वकर्माको गुह्य पूजा गरिन्छ । त्यसबेला विश्वकर्मालाई दुईवटा भेडा बलि दिई भोज खाने गरिन्छ । वर्षको एकपटक ज्याथाका प्रजापतिहरूले बाजा, नाच, अभिनय सिकाउने नासःद्यःको पूजा गर्छन् । नासःद्यःको पूजा गर्ने दिन चाहिँ निश्चित छैन । गुठीयारहरूको अनुकुलता हेरी हिउँदमा यो पूजा गरिन्छ, तर आइतवार वा विहिवारको दिन नै पार्नुपर्ने नियम रहेको छ ।* काठमाडौं, ललितपुर र भक्तपुर तीनै शहरमा ज्याथा टोल रहेका छन् र प्रजापति (कुम्हाले)हरू बसोबास गर्छन् । तीनै शहरका प्रजापतिहरू गणेशलाई विश्वकर्मा मानी पूजा गर्छन् । हेर्नुस्, भक्तपुरको जेठा गणेश मन्दिर (BKT0510) ।  ललितपुरको ज्याथा टोलमा रहेको गणेशलाई विश्वकर्मा भनी सम्बोधन गरिएको अभिलेखको लागि हेर्नुस्,  D. Vajrācārya VS 2056, p. 93, inscr. no. 50

historical_events.event_description: Prajāpati Jeta, Amita, and Dhana, among others, collectively built aphalcarest house for their lineage deity Viśvakarmā to the east of the temple. Thephalcāmention in this inscription is the god-house (dyaḥchẽ) east of the temple. Thedyaḥchẽwas previously aphalcāand was dismantled in 1988 CE (VS 2045) to be converted into adyaḥchẽ, which has now been rented out.

The Aṣṭamī Sevā Guthi, a religious trust of 28 people including the guru of the Jyāthā Ṭola Devānanda Prajāpati, senior Tuisiṃ, and manager Visuṃdla, constructed another rest house (sataḥ) in front of the temple.
Beṣāsiṃha, Dhanaontasiṃha, Dhanasiddhi, and others built anotherphalcaand installed an inscription bearing their own figures.

A donor erected a rest house (phalcā) in memory of his late father, Mahaṃtasī, and dedicated it to him, his mother, wife, and son, with prayers for their eternal peace. The donor's name was unfortunately illegible, as it was obscured by concrete.

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of new statue of Viśvakarmā
historical_events.event_description: Matyaṃsiṃ Prajāpati and his wife, Manamati, along with their sons and grandsons, replaced the old, worn-out statue of Viśvakarmā with a new one, wishing for the eternal peace of their deceased family members. They also established a religious trust with land and money for the statue’s anniversary rituals.

historical_events.event_name: Repair of the statue of Viśvakarmā
historical_events.event_description: The Digusivā Guthi, a religious trust responsible for serving the Prajāpati community's lineage deity, headed by Cidhisiṃha, renovated the dilapidated statue of Viśvakarmā and gilded it. The statue was taken around the city before being established inside the sanctum.
The Pañcadāna Guthi of the Prajāpatis in Jyāthā, with financial assistance from the Kathmandu Metropolitan City, renovated the dilapidated temple.
